pinterest.title: Planning a Wedding in Crete: Months, Ceremony Times and Summer Heat
pinterest.description: On long-term averages, May and September bring highs of about 24 to 27 degrees on Crete with few rain days, while July and August run above 30 degrees in the Chania area. Venues set their own windows: Minos Palace gives April to November for eastern Crete, and Nana Princess suggests evening ceremonies in high summer. Our guide sets out the month-by-month table, ceremony times and how to plan for heat and wind.

pinterest.title: Wedding in Crete: East, Centre or West? Choosing Your End of the Island
pinterest.description: Crete runs about 260 kilometres end to end, so choose your end of the island before your venue. The east around Elounda and Agios Nikolaos is resort country, Heraklion keeps the main airport close, and the west holds the old towns of Chania and Rethymno. Venues range from Elounda Beach's private chapel to Avra Imperial at Kolymvari and the hilltop garden at Sea View by En Kipo in Chania.

pinterest.title: What Drives the Cost of a Wedding in Crete: Rooms, Exclusive Use and Extras
pinterest.description: Two Crete quotes with the same guest list can land far apart. Season, minimum stays, exclusive use, venue fee or package, extras priced separately and document costs all play a part. The Elounda Collection ties its packages to a minimum three-night stay, and Elounda Beach lists photography, video and flowers for the wedding location outside its indicative package. Take our ten questions to every venue and ask for the answers in writing.

slides: Crete is on your shortlist. Now the questions are practical ones: which month, which end of the island, and what moves the cost.
Month: on long-term averages, May and September bring highs of about 24 to 27 degrees with few rain days. July and August run above 30 degrees in the Chania area.
Ceremony time moves with the season. Nana Princess at Chersonissos suggests 16:00 to 18:00 in April, May and October, and 18:30 to 20:00 in July and August.
Choose the end of the island before the venue. The east is resort country around Elounda and Agios Nikolaos. The west centres on the old towns of Chania and Rethymno.
Book the airport to suit the venue. From Agios Nikolaos, Chania Airport is about a 180-minute drive. Land at the wrong end and arrival day is spent on the road.
Read the terms behind each quote: minimum stays, exclusive use, venue fee or package, extras priced separately, and who pays for Apostilles, translation and official fees.
Weighing up Crete? Send us your month, guest count and the venues you have in mind, and a Wedded Advisor will talk it through with you. Link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Thinking about a wedding in Crete?

Crete is the largest island in Greece, with more than 1,000 kilometres of coastline, and it is not one backdrop but a string of quite different places. In the east, Elounda faces its lagoon and Spinalonga. In the west, Chania's Venetian harbour sits under the Egyptian lighthouse, and Rethymno lies beneath its Fortezza.

Our new guide works through the practical questions. It sets out average highs and rain days month by month for Heraklion and the Chania area, the ceremony times venues suggest as the season warms, and how to plan for summer heat and wildfire season from June to September.

It also covers how to choose the end of the island by where your guests will land, six venues from Elounda Beach to Sea View by En Kipo, and what drives the cost: rooms and minimum stays, exclusive use, venue fee or package, extras priced separately and the paperwork for a legal wedding. It closes with ten questions to ask every venue in writing.

Planning your own Crete wedding? Send us a message with your month, guest count and the venues you are weighing up. Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit. Full guide at the link in our bio.
